title: Choose the bench structure
question: Bolder hand. The roll assigned Summoned stage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Summoned stage
options.thesis: The stage never moves; a persistent summon field calls a tool into it by name.
options.viewport: Identity and a summon field sit in an unmoving chrome; the current tool's existing interior fills the stage; hash still lands on a tool.
options.risk: A growing set becomes unbrowseable if summon is the only way to notice a tool exists.

raised.raise: Place never moves; only which tool is lit in the stage.
Switching a tool does not rearrange the chrome.

options.label: Drafting arm
options.thesis: Identity is a clamp that never leaves the board; switching tools changes the instrument in the arm.
options.viewport: A persistent arm along one edge holds identity and the tool switcher; the paper — the current tool interior — stays registered in the same gates.
options.risk: The arm can read as decoration if the switcher is not the obvious instrument change.

options.label: Fold-out handle
options.thesis: One tool unfolds from a persistent handle; the others stay nested until called.
options.viewport: A compact handle of identity plus nested tools sits on one edge; the active tool unfolds into the same stage and folds back without leaving.
options.risk: Nesting can hide tools you reach for by name, the same failure clustering had.

options.label: Lit-cell mask
options.thesis: The layout is a rigid mask of cells; place never moves, only which cell is lit.
options.viewport: Every tool occupies a fixed cell in one mask; inactive tools remain as ghosts; the active interior fills the stage.
options.case: The unmoving mask is the raise; a segment alphabet is not how these forms work.
options.kept: Place never moves; only which tool is lit.
options.risk: Reads as a clock face, not a CSS bench.

options.label: Glyph grid
options.thesis: The world is one character grid; you move the camera and the view re-renders in place.
options.viewport: The whole shell is one grid; switching tools re-renders the stage without changing place.
options.case: Loses on audience identification: a glyph sculpture is not this bench.
options.kept: Results live in the same grid as the work, not on a separate page.
options.risk: Turns a utility bench into a demo.

options.label: Stacked cases
options.thesis: Tools are stacked cases; you pull one into the working position and open it.
options.viewport: A wall of labeled cases; the selected one slides into the stage while others stay stacked as labels.
options.case: Pulling a case open is still destination navigation, which this brief forbids.
options.kept: Unused tools remain visible as labels while one occupies the stage.
options.risk: The lid-open is a page change wearing a box.

options.label: Cut blocks
options.thesis: You cut a working block from a mass and handle it while it stays live.
options.viewport: Tools as blocks in one mass; the working block stays live on the stage without a page change.
options.case: Surreal quarry topology fails audience identification and product clarity.
options.kept: The working tool stays live while you switch; nothing unmounts into a new place.

options.label: Focus wall
options.thesis: Rows of tools; the focused one expands and the rest of the wall dims.
options.viewport: A wall of tool tiles; focus expands one interior; neighbors dim in place.
options.case: This is the eliminated inventory, reworded as a catalog wall.
options.kept: Unused tools recede without becoming a different place.
options.risk: Browses a library instead of working a bench.

options.label: Free captions
options.thesis: Chrome is free-placed labels keyed to the active tool, not a nav band.
options.viewport: The tool interior fills the frame; identity and switcher land as captions that do not occupy a lower-third.
options.case: Free-placed switching is worse for a named lookup than a stable control.
options.kept: Switching a tool does not rearrange the chrome.
options.risk: Makes a utility feel like a broadcast overlay.
